IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Senators Fraser, B. Sheldon, Carlson, McAuliffe and Kohl-Welles

Bill.BriefDescription: Ensuring the quality and availability of educational interpreters.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to educational interpreters; and creating newsections.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that the Washingtonprofessional educator standards board has advisory responsibilities oncertain educational issues, including certification issues. Thelegislature further finds that there is currently no requirement foreducational interpreters for deaf and hard of hearing students to becertified or to meet standardized qualifications or competencies.

By November 30, 2004, the Washingtonprofessional educator standards board shall conduct a comprehensivereview and analysis of the following options and make recommendationsto the governor, the legislature, the superintendent of publicinstruction, and the state board of education regarding the followingoptions: (1) Requiring national or state certification for all educationalinterpreters for deaf students and hard of hearing students; p. 1 SB 5105 (2) Designating educational interpreters as an education staffassistant; (3) Requiring the state board of education to establishcompetencies for educational interpreters; and (4) Any other option that the Washington professional educatorstandards board deems viable to increase and maintain the quality andavailability of educational interpreters in a fiscally responsiblemanner.
